narr: A strong nocturnal low-level jet interacting with a nearly stationary frontal boundary triggered a Mesoscale Convective System (MCS) over northern Missouri during the pre-dawn hours of June 17th. The large thunderstorm cluster tracked east-southeastward along the boundary, producing significant wind damage and flash flooding. The storms were focused along and southeast of a Rushville...to Springfield...to Shelbyville...to Robinson line. Numerous trees and power lines were blown down. In addition, very heavy rainfall of 3 to 5 inches along and south of a Jacksonville to Effingham line created pockets of flash flooding.
ev: Several streets were flooded in Pana.
Apple Creek spilled out of its banks and flowed across Route 111 southwest of Waverly.
Water was flowing across Route 104 northwest of Franklin.
Water was flowing across US-40 and US-45 in Effingham.
The Fayette Avenue underpass in Effingham was closed due to high water.
Water was flowing across 1710th Street northwest of Teutopolis. Both bridges were underwater.

Water was flowing across Route 128 north of Cowden.
